editorial:
Imagine spending a whole day in New York City just trying to help a friend out, only to have the world change around you. You follow Khan, a guy who agrees to cover some pot deals for his buddy Jerry on a very specific day: November 8, 2016. The vibe is super raw and grounded because it was shot in real time. It feels less like a polished Hollywood movie and more like you are just walking alongside Khan as he navigates the city streets, dealing with customers and the general chaos of a busy Tuesday. 

What makes this one special is how the real-world election results start leaking into the script. The acting feels natural, and the tension builds as the characters react to the news on their phones in real time. It is a bit slow in some spots, but that is the point of the real-time format. If you like indie films that feel like a social experiment, you will love this. It is best enjoyed streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: As the day ends, the focus shifts from the drug deals to the shock of the election results. You see the characters struggle to process the news, which turns the simple favor for Jerry into a moment of personal reflection. The movie wraps up by showing how a normal day of work was completely overshadowed by a historical event. It ends on a quiet, thoughtful note, leaving you to think about how life changes in an instant.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves raw indie films and stories about real-life moments.
